hookRows.body_you:
The Capricorn Moon keeps the day standing; finishing things is how it feels safe. For two and a half days, that is the gift. The hard thing gets handled. Care shows up as reliability; the promise kept, the practical problem quietly solved.

The trouble starts in Capricorn's shadow: fear running the show in a suit. Composure becomes suppression. The mountain gets climbed without anyone asking whose it is, and the standard being met belongs to someone else entirely. The one who handles everything never gets asked how they are, partly because they never answer. Rest does not have to be earned through exhaustion. Capricorn doesn't need more proof. It needs the feeling to count as part of the day.

hookRows.body_you:
The Scorpio Moon names what has been circling unsaid. For two and a half days, that is the gift. The door closes and the difficult conversation finally finishes. The question avoided all month gets asked. Admitting how hard something has been stops feeling like weakness.

The trouble starts in Scorpio's shadow: the fear of being left with nothing. Every silence gets filled with the worst explanation. A short reply gets reread for what it hid. Jealousy dresses up as insight, and a private feeling gets guarded like evidence. Scorpio doesn't need the whole truth excavated at once. It needs one honest sentence said out loud, and most of it comes down to trust.

hookRows.body_you:
The Aquarius Moon zooms out; distance is how it sorts a feeling. For two and a half days, that is the gift. The week reads as a pattern instead of a storm. A feeling becomes information. The loop a relationship keeps running finally has a name.

The trouble starts in Aquarius' shadow: the view from the fringe. Distance turns into absence. A feeling gets analyzed instead of answered, and the observation about the pattern arrives where the warmth was needed. Being the one who sees it all starts feeling like a reason to stay outside it all. Detachment isn't enlightenment when it's really just dissociation. Aquarius doesn't need us above the room. It needs the clear view brought back down into it.

hookRows.body_you:
The Aries Moon strips the delay between feeling and action. For two and a half days, that is the gift; we know how we feel immediately and can say it without a week of rehearsal. Courage comes cheaper. The thing that needed saying gets said today.

The trouble starts in Aries' shadow: it wants what it wants immediately. The first flash gets the final word. A sharp reply starts a fight the feeling did not need, and seeing it from the other side becomes impossible for exactly as long as it matters. Under the impatience there is usually something unacknowledged, and it comes out as anger. Aries doesn't need us to act instantly. It needs us to act honestly.

hookRows.body_you:
The Cancer Moon turns the care up, and time with the ones who count as family does more than any plan. For two and a half days, that is the gift. The meal gets cooked instead of ordered. The person whose silence has been noticed gets the call. The shell is there for anyone who needs an evening inside it.

The trouble starts in Cancer's shadow: care with strings attached. Everyone else's comfort gets managed while our own request goes unsaid, and the unsaid part turns passive aggressive. Helping becomes a way of keeping someone needing us. A change of tone gets taken personally before anyone asks what happened. Cancer doesn't need us to mother everyone. It needs the care to point inward too, boundaries included.

hookRows.body_you:
The Gemini Moon opens doors, and asking the questions is how it takes care of itself. It is a time to approach life with playfulness, curiosity, and childlike wonder. For two and a half days, that is the gift. The stuck conversation finds its opening. The right message arrives for the person who needed it. The thing that felt unsayable turns out to take one sentence.

The trouble starts in Gemini's shadow: all talk, no commitment. Plans get made warmly and dropped quietly. The story about someone gets told to everyone but them. Talking about the decision replaces making it. Without grounding, curiosity becomes avoidance. Words become noise. Gemini doesn't need us to say everything. It needs us to say the one thing that has been waiting, to the person it belongs to; and sometimes that person is us.

hookRows.body_you:
The Virgo Moon turns unease into a list; clearing the desk settles the nerves more than talking about them. Virgo moon is good for organizing. For two and a half days, that is the gift; the vague bad feeling becomes one solvable step, the small discomfort ignored for weeks finally gets fixed, and love gets shown by quietly handling something practical.

The trouble starts in Virgo's shadow: critical of everything, ourselves first. The flaw gets all the attention so the feeling never gets its turn. Help arrives as criticism with good intentions. Service becomes self-sacrifice, and doing everything for everyone eventually shows the real problem: none of the care is aimed at ourselves. Virgo doesn't need everything perfect. It needs one real thing handled, and the rest left alone.
